definitionEn: a fast, always-on connection that lets you use the internet
situation: You talk about a fast home or office internet connection that can handle video calls and large downloads without delay.

examples.text: Half the street was left without [[broadband]] after engineers accidentally cut a cable.
We switched providers because our old [[broadband]] kept dropping out during video calls.
Rural villages are still waiting for reliable [[broadband]] to reach their area.

texts: Cafés without decent [[broadband]] are losing customers to ones with fast wifi.
The government promised every household [[broadband]] by the end of the decade.
Without [[broadband]], streaming a two-hour film would take all night.

badCollocation.noteRu: Broadband — это тип интернет-соединения, а не устройство с кнопкой. Включают router (роутер) или wifi, а не broadband.

collocationTask.prompt: the council plans to ___ broadband to every farm in the region
collocationTask.explanationRu: С broadband сочетается extend (расширить зону покрытия). Enlarge, widen и lengthen говорят о физическом размере предмета, а не о зоне охвата сети.

nuance.text: Our [[broadband]] is fast, but the wifi signal barely reaches the back bedroom.
nuance.explanationRu: Broadband — это сам интернет-канал, который заходит в дом. Wifi — беспроводная раздача этого интернета внутри помещения через роутер.

reverse.text: The router's [[wifi]] only reaches the kitchen, so we need a signal booster upstairs.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь речь о беспроводном сигнале внутри дома — wifi, а не о самом интернет-канале.

fixIt.text: The engineer is coming tomorrow to fix our [[wifi]], because the connection keeps cutting out completely.
fixIt.explanationRu: Инженер провайдера чинит broadband — сам канал, по которому приходит интернет. Wifi — это раздача сигнала внутри дома через свой роутер.

rewrite.original: The company laid new fibre-optic cables to give the whole town fast internet access.
rewrite.frame: The company laid new fibre-optic cables to give the whole town fast ____ access.
rewrite.explanationRu: «Fast broadband access» — стандартное сочетание для быстрого интернет-соединения.

definitionEn: a computer program used for looking at websites
situation: You talk about the software on a computer or phone that you use to open and look at web pages.

examples.text: The bank's website looks broken in this old [[browser]], so try opening it in a different one.
Clearing the cache and cookies in your [[browser]] can fix a lot of loading problems.
Some employees are still using an outdated [[browser]] that the IT department no longer supports.

texts: Try updating your [[browser]] before reporting the bug.
My phone's default [[browser]] loads pages faster than the one I used to use.
Not every [[browser]] displays this animation correctly.

badCollocation.noteRu: Browser — программа для просмотра сайтов на устройстве, а не сам интернет. «Нет интернета» — no internet или no broadband, а не no browser.

collocationTask.prompt: you should ___ your browser regularly to fix bugs and security holes
collocationTask.explanationRu: Обновляют программу — update your browser. Refresh/reload значит «перезагрузить страницу», renew — «продлить» (подписку, контракт).

nuance.text: I opened my [[browser]] and typed the address straight into the bar, without using Google.
nuance.explanationRu: Browser (например, Chrome) — программа для выхода в интернет; search engine (например, Google) — сервис для поиска внутри интернета.

reverse.text: I typed my question into a [[search engine]] instead of going straight to the site.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь именно ищут через сервис поиска, а не просто открывают программу для интернета.

fixIt.text: I can't find that bookmark — which [[search engine]] were you using when you saved it?
fixIt.explanationRu: Закладки (bookmarks) сохраняются в browser (Chrome, Firefox), а не в search engine — поисковике вроде Google.

wordFormation.text: Most people now do their shopping through an app rather than a [[browser]].

reply.context: A friend texts you: "My laptop feels so slow lately, any idea why?"
options: Have you tried clearing the cache in your browser? That usually speeds things up a lot.
Yeah, your browser is probably full of dust — try opening the case and cleaning it.
One must ascertain whether the aforementioned browser requires a firmware update, I should think.
reply.explanationRu: Browser — программа, у которой не бывает «пыли» внутри. Третий вариант звучит слишком официально для сообщения другу.

definitionEn: extremely harsh, violent or unpleasant, without any gentleness
senseNote: Кроме прямого насилия, brutal описывает и предельно жёсткие, некомфортные вещи: brutal honesty, a brutal schedule.
situation: You describe an attack, a punishment, or something else so harsh and unpleasant that it seems to ignore any kindness.

examples.text: Critics called the film's final battle scene [[brutal]], almost too violent to watch.
I'd rather have [[brutal]] honesty from my editor than empty praise.
New recruits are warned that the training schedule is [[brutal]], with almost no rest days.

texts: The critics were [[brutal]] about her debut novel.
Competition in the taxi industry has become [[brutal]] since the new app arrived.
January in this city is [[brutal]] — icy wind straight off the sea.

badCollocation.noteRu: Brutal — про насилие или крайнюю жёсткость. Обычную ошибку называют careless или costly, а не brutal.

collocationTask.prompt: the coach gave the team some ___ feedback after the loss
collocationTask.explanationRu: Резкую, жёсткую критику называют brutal feedback. Tasty, spacious и musical по смыслу со словом feedback не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The war crimes tribunal described the massacre as [[brutal]] beyond any military necessity.
nuance.explanationRu: Brutal — крайне жестокий по масштабу или силе действия. Cruel — жестокий по намерению, специально причиняющий боль. Здесь акцент на масштабе насилия.

reverse.text: Some say it was [[cruel]] to keep the news from her for so long.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь дело не в физическом насилии, а в намеренном, бессердечном поступке — это cruel, а не brutal.

fixIt.text: The dictator's regime was infamous for its [[aggressive]] crackdowns on any form of protest.
fixIt.explanationRu: О жестоких силовых разгонах говорят brutal crackdowns. Aggressive — скорее об агрессивном поведении или тоне, а не о жестоком насилии.

wordFormation.text: Human rights groups condemned the [[brutality]] of the police response.

reply.context: A friend asks: "How was your first week at the new gym?"
options: Brutal, honestly — I could barely walk after the first session.
Brutal — the gym was totally packed today, standing room only.
The physical exertion demanded of novice participants was, regrettably, of a rather brutal nature.
reply.explanationRu: Brutal — «очень тяжёлый, безжалостный», а не «переполненный». Третий вариант звучит как официальный отчёт, а не ответ другу.

definitionEn: an informal partner who helps or supports you with a task or activity
senseNote: Здесь — «напарник» в системе buddy system (в школе, при нырянии, в спорте), а не просто «приятель» — это более базовое значение.
situation: A school, gym or programme pairs you with another person so that you can help, check on and support each other.

examples.text: Every new diver is paired with an experienced [[buddy]] for safety underwater.
My gym [[buddy]] texts me every morning to make sure I actually show up.
The school assigns each new student a [[buddy]] to help them settle in during the first week.

texts: She's been my running [[buddy]] for three years now.
New employees are given a [[buddy]] for their first month.
Without a study [[buddy]], it's hard to stay motivated before exams.

badCollocation.text: hire a [[buddy]] to check your tax return
badCollocation.noteRu: Buddy — неформальный напарник для поддержки, а не платный специалист. Налоговую декларацию проверяет accountant, а не buddy.

collocationTask.prompt: the gym pairs up beginners with a more experienced ___ for their first few sessions
collocationTask.explanationRu: Напарника по тренировкам называют buddy. Referee судит матчи, cashier работает на кассе, librarian — в библиотеке.

nuance.text: On your first day, a [[buddy]] will show you where everything is and eat lunch with you.
nuance.explanationRu: Buddy — напарник твоего же уровня, который просто помогает освоиться. Mentor — более опытный наставник, который развивает твои профессиональные навыки.

reverse.text: Later in the year, you'll also be assigned a senior [[mentor]] to guide your career development.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь речь про наставника по карьере более высокого уровня — mentor, а не равный по статусу buddy.

fixIt.text: For my first week at the hospital, I was given a [[mentor]] who mostly just showed me where the coffee machine was.
fixIt.explanationRu: Того, кто просто помогает освоиться в первую неделю, называют buddy. Mentor обычно развивает карьеру, а не показывает офис.

reply.context: A colleague messages: "I'm starting a new job on Monday and I'm nervous about the first day."
options: Don't worry — most companies give you a buddy for the first week who'll show you the ropes.
Don't worry, your manager will be your buddy from day one, checking every report you write.
Rest assured, an appointed colleague shall be designated to assist you during the initial period, as per company policy.
reply.explanationRu: Buddy — неформальный равный напарник, а не начальник, который всё проверяет. Третий ответ звучит как официальная инструкция.

definitionEn: something that protects against harm by absorbing a shock or giving extra time or space
senseNote: Здесь — «запас, подушка безопасности» (финансы, время, отношения), а не техническое значение buffer в программировании (временная память).
situation: You describe extra money, time or space kept in reserve so that a sudden problem does not cause serious harm.

examples.text: Financial advisors recommend keeping three months' salary as a [[buffer]] in case you lose your job.
We booked an extra night in the city as a [[buffer]] in case our flight was delayed.
The park acts as a green [[buffer]] between the motorway and the residential streets.

texts: Try to keep a small [[buffer]] in your monthly budget for emergencies.
The ceasefire created a narrow [[buffer]] between the two armies.
Leaving a ten-minute [[buffer]] between meetings stops the whole day running late.

badCollocation.noteRu: Buffer — запас денег, времени или пространства «на всякий случай». Про удачу говорят luck или a stroke of luck, а не buffer.

collocationTask.prompt: savers are advised to build up a financial ___ before investing in anything risky
collocationTask.explanationRu: Денежный запас «на чёрный день» — a financial buffer. Income, salary и budget называют сами деньги или план расходов, а не запас на случай проблем.

nuance.text: A cash [[buffer]] softens the blow of unexpected expenses like a broken boiler.
nuance.explanationRu: Buffer — денежный запас, смягчающий удар от непредвиденных трат. Backup — запасной вариант или копия на случай, если основной откажет (backup generator, backup plan).

reverse.text: Always keep a [[backup]] generator in case the power goes out during the storm.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь нужен именно запасной, дублирующий источник энергии — backup, а не денежный или временной запас buffer.

fixIt.text: Financial advisors suggest keeping three months of expenses as a [[backup]] in a separate savings account.
fixIt.explanationRu: Денежный запас на случай проблем — buffer. Backup — дублирующая копия или запасной вариант, а не финансовая подушка.

rewrite.original: We left home an hour early in case there was traffic on the motorway.
rewrite.frame: We left home an hour early to give ourselves a ____ in case there was traffic.

definitionEn: the largest or main part of something
senseNote: Здесь — «основная часть» (the bulk of); значения «крупный размер, масса» (his enormous bulk) и «оптом» (buy in bulk) не рассматриваем.
situation: You talk about the largest part or majority of something, such as money, work or a period of time.

examples.text: The [[bulk]] of the company's profits comes from just two products.
She spent the [[bulk]] of her twenties travelling around South America.
Volunteers handled the [[bulk]] of the clean-up after the storm.

texts: The [[bulk]] of our budget goes on rent.
He had already eaten the [[bulk]] of the pizza before we arrived.
The [[bulk]] of the traffic clears by nine in the morning.

badCollocation.noteRu: О большинстве людей говорят the majority of people или most people. Bulk используют для денег, работы, времени, но не для количества людей.

collocationTask.prompt: volunteers, not paid staff, did the ___ of the fundraising work
collocationTask.explanationRu: Основную часть работы называют the bulk of the work. Length, height и width — это физические размеры, они не подходят к объёму работы.

nuance.text: The [[bulk]] of the paperwork was finished before lunch.
nuance.explanationRu: Bulk обычно используют с неисчисляемыми существительными (paperwork, money, time). Majority — с исчисляемыми, чаще о людях: the majority of voters.

reverse.text: The [[majority]] of voters supported the new law.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь речь о людях (voters) — исчисляемое существительное во множественном числе, поэтому majority, а не bulk.

fixIt.text: The [[majority]] of the company's debt was paid off within two years.
fixIt.explanationRu: Debt — неисчисляемое существительное, с ним говорят the bulk of the debt. Majority чаще используют с исчисляемыми (people, voters).

wordFormation.text: The [[bulky]] old television barely fit through the door.

rewrite.original: We spent almost all of our budget on marketing this year.
rewrite.frame: The ____ of our budget went on marketing this year.
rewrite.explanationRu: Bulk — «основная часть» (обычно про деньги, время, работу).

definitionEn: a heavy responsibility, duty or worry that is difficult to deal with
senseNote: Здесь — переносное значение «тяжёлая обязанность, груз забот» (financial burden, burden of proof), а не буквальный тяжёлый груз, который несут на себе.
situation: You describe a duty, cost or worry that is heavy and difficult for a person or group to deal with.

examples.text: Rising rent has become a serious [[burden]] for young families in the city.
In most courts, the [[burden]] of proof lies with the prosecution.
Caring for an elderly parent alone can become an emotional [[burden]].

texts: New taxes have added to the [[burden]] on small businesses.
She refused to let guilt become a daily [[burden]].
The extra paperwork is a real [[burden]] for teachers already short on time.

badCollocation.noteRu: Бремя не «решают» (solve), а облегчают или снимают: ease/lighten the burden. Solve подходит к problem, а не к burden.

collocationTask.prompt: campaigners want the government to ___ the burden of childcare costs on working parents
collocationTask.explanationRu: Бремя облегчают — ease the burden. Solve решают проблему, answer отвечают на вопрос, repair чинят поломку — с burden они не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The new regulations have placed an unfair [[burden]] on small shopkeepers.
nuance.explanationRu: Burden — тяжёлая, часто несправедливая обязанность или груз забот. Load — более нейтральное «объём работы, груз», без оттенка несправедливости.

reverse.text: Her teaching [[load]] this term is three classes a day, which feels quite manageable.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь просто нейтральный «объём работы» без оттенка тяжести и несправедливости — load, а не burden.

fixIt.text: Small shopkeepers say the new paperwork rules have placed an unfair [[load]] on their businesses.
fixIt.explanationRu: Несправедливую, тяжёлую обязанность называют burden. Load — более нейтральный «объём работы», без оттенка несправедливости.

wordFormation.text: Working two jobs while studying full-time proved utterly [[burdensome]].

reply.context: A friend says: "My parents want me to look after my grandmother every weekend now."
options: That sounds like a real burden, especially on top of your job. Can your siblings share it?
Wow, what a burden — free breakfast every weekend, you're so lucky!
Indeed, such a familial obligation constitutes a considerable burden upon one's personal schedule.
reply.explanationRu: Burden — что-то тяжёлое и неприятное, а не приятный бонус. Третий ответ звучит слишком официально для разговора с другом.

definitionEn: an official system with many complicated rules and processes that can seem slow or unnecessary
situation: You complain about official rules, forms and procedures in government or a large organisation that make simple things slow.

examples.text: Opening a small business here means wading through months of [[bureaucracy]].
The hospital's own [[bureaucracy]] delayed her test results by nearly two weeks.
Critics say the ministry has grown into a vast, unaccountable [[bureaucracy]].

texts: Getting a visa here involves endless [[bureaucracy]].
The company's internal [[bureaucracy]] slows down even simple decisions.
He blamed [[bureaucracy]] for the months of delay on his claim.

badCollocation.noteRu: Бюрократию не «решают» — reduce bureaucracy или cut through the bureaucracy, а не solve.

collocationTask.prompt: the new online system was designed to cut through unnecessary ___
collocationTask.explanationRu: Волокиту, лишние формальности называют bureaucracy. Scenery (пейзаж), currency (валюта) и harmony (гармония) по смыслу сюда не подходят.

nuance.text: Local business owners blame the town's [[bureaucracy]] for driving away new investment.
nuance.explanationRu: Bureaucracy обычно звучит критично: излишне сложная, медленная система правил. Administration — нейтральное слово для системы управления, без критики.

reverse.text: The university's admissions [[administration]] processes over fifty thousand applications every year.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь просто нейтральное описание работы системы, без критики за медлительность — administration, а не bureaucracy.

fixIt.text: Local shop owners blame the town's [[administration]] for burying every new project under months of pointless paperwork.
fixIt.explanationRu: Когда критикуют именно медлительность и лишние правила, говорят bureaucracy, а не нейтральное administration.

wordFormation.text: He spent thirty years working his way up through the state [[bureaucracy]].

reply.context: A friend vents: "I've been trying to get my address changed on my ID for six weeks!"
options: That's classic bureaucracy — so many offices make you fill out the same form five times.
That's such bureaucracy of them, ignoring your calls like that!
Such institutional inefficiency is indeed a matter deserving of formal escalation, one imagines.
reply.explanationRu: Bureaucracy — существительное, нельзя сказать «bureaucracy of them». Третий ответ звучит как официальный отчёт, а не сочувствие другу.

definitionEn: involving complicated official rules and processes, often seen as slow or excessive
situation: You describe a process, system or organisation that is full of slow, complicated official rules and forms.

examples.text: Renewing a passport here is a famously [[bureaucratic]] process involving five separate offices.
Employees complained that the new expense system was overly [[bureaucratic]].
Compared with the state hospital, the private clinic felt fast and refreshingly free of [[bureaucratic]] delay.

texts: Getting reimbursed here is a slow, [[bureaucratic]] nightmare.
The council's planning process is notoriously [[bureaucratic]].
Even simple requests get lost in [[bureaucratic]] procedure.

badCollocation.noteRu: Bureaucratic описывает процессы, системы и организации (a bureaucratic process), а не настроение человека — плохое настроение это a bad mood.

collocationTask.prompt: getting a simple permit here means struggling through a hopelessly ___ system
collocationTask.explanationRu: Излишне формальную, медленную систему правил называют bureaucratic. Musical, coastal и seasonal по смыслу со словом system не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Getting a simple signature approved took three [[bureaucratic]] weeks of forms and stamps.
nuance.explanationRu: Bureaucratic звучит критично про излишне сложные, медленные правила. Official — нейтральное «одобренный организацией», без критики за медлительность.

reverse.text: You'll need an [[official]] letter from the university to open a student bank account.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь просто нужен документ, одобренный организацией, без критики за волокиту — official, а не bureaucratic.

fixIt.text: Renewing my visa turned into a slow, [[official]] nightmare involving five separate government desks.
fixIt.explanationRu: Когда речь о медленной, чрезмерно формальной процедуре, нужно bureaucratic. Official — просто «официальный», без оттенка критики за волокиту.

wordFormation.text: Small charities often pride themselves on being far less [[bureaucratic]] than government departments.

rewrite.original: It took five different offices and dozens of forms just to change my address.
rewrite.frame: Changing my address turned into an incredibly ____ business, with five offices and dozens of forms.
rewrite.explanationRu: Bureaucratic — «излишне формальный, волокитный»: подходящее слово для описания этой ситуации.
